annotation.title_clean: Florida Statutes s. 330.41 – Unmanned Aircraft Systems Act
annotation.title_en: Florida Statutes s. 330.41 – Unmanned Aircraft Systems Act
named_instruments_referenced: FAA Extension, Safety and Security Act of 2016
annotation.summary_en: Florida's Unmanned Aircraft Systems Act (s. 330.41, 2026 Florida Statutes). It gives the state, rather than local governments, authority over drone operations, protects drone delivery ports from local bans, and makes it a crime to fly drones over or near critical infrastructure, schools, agricultural lands and private property, with stated exemptions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Authority to regulate unmanned aircraft system operations is vested in the state; local ordinances on drone design and operation are barred
Political subdivisions may not block drone delivery services based on the location of their drone ports
Operating drones over or near critical infrastructure facilities is a third-degree felony unless the flight is FAA-authorized or otherwise exempt
Flying drones over schools, agricultural lands or private property (with intent to harass) is a misdemeanor; recording video raises the penalties
Exemptions apply to government entities, law enforcement complying with s. 934.50, and owners or persons with their consent
